title: Grateful Dead Live at Oregon Country Fair on 1982-08-28
lineage: Cassette  (Nakamichi DR-1) -> Sound Devices 744T (24bit/96k) -> Adobe Audition v3.0 -> Samplitude Professional v11.03 -> FLAC/16

ai_review.summary: Fantastic soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1982 show with a smoking “Other One” and standout Althea/Black Peter, despite a shaky second‑set opening.
ai_review.review: The recording is an immaculate soundboard tape that delivers crystal‑clear detail and a deep low‑end punch. Musically the concert shines in the second half – The Other One, Althea, Black Peter and China Rider are repeatedly praised – while the early part of set II (Day Job, West LA, Far From Me) is seen as uneven. Overall the band’s energy is described as “on fire,” with Brent Mydland’s organ work especially highlighted.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating is 4.0/5; most comments are enthusiastic about performance and note excellent soundboard quality, outweighing a few set‑list criticisms.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Consistently described as crisp, fantastic, immaculate and with strong bottom end; no significant dropouts or noise reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Set I is praised as sizzlin' and tight; Set II opens with a series of weaker debut choices (Day Job, West LA, Far From Me) that make the flow feel disjointed before the band recovers with high‑impact performances.

band_member_comments.Jerry: High‑octane leads and nonstop soloing ("soloing through intermission"); occasional lyric improvisation noted but overall energy praised.
band_member_comments.Phil: Strong, “lots o Phil” bass presence that drives the show; described as powerful and energetic.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent Mydland’s organ on The Other One called out‑of‑this‑world, bordering on Black Sabbath intensity; consistently highlighted for inspiration.
